summary: Maha Chakri Sirindhorn specializes in Indology, history, archaeology, and Sinology. She studied at Chitralada School, Chulalongkorn University, Silpakorn University under Satya Vrat Shastri, Srinakharinwirot University, the Asian Institute of Technology, and Peking University.

Mahasi Sayadaw was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under traditional teachers Mingun Jetawun Sayadaw U Narada, Aletawya Sayadaw, and Thelon Sayadaw. He served as abbot at Mawlamyine Monastery, resident teacher at Mahasi Sasana Yeiktha, and founded the Insight Meditation Society.

Mahendranath Gupta worked in religious studies and Indology after studying at Hare School, Presidency University, and the University of Calcutta. He held a professorship at Ripon College and a post at Surendranath College.

Mahesh A. Deokar is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He has served as professor and department head at Savitribai Phule Pune University, and as a regional representative for the Pali Text Society.
Mahesh Chandra Nyayaratna Bhattacharyya was an Indology scholar who studied under Edward Byles Cowell. He served as principal of Sanskrit College and University.

Mahinda Deegalle specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Ceylon, Harvard University, and the University of Chicago under Frank E. Reynolds, Wendy Doniger, and Diana L. Eck, later holding posts at McGill, Colgate, and Bath Spa universities.
Mahiro Ito is a Buddhist studies scholar who succeeded Norihiko Tanaka in 2021. He has held professorships at Bukkyo University and Kyoto Bunkyo University.

Maho Iuchi is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at Otani University around 2003–2008. She was attested as a guest researcher at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies in 2010.
Mai Mishiro is a researcher in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Mishiro held posts at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2011) and Waseda University (attested 2016).

Makio Takemura is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and under Ryōmin Akizuki. His academic career includes professorships at Mie University, the University of Tsukuba, and serving as president of Toyo University (2009–2020).

Makio Ueno specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning a PhD from Otani University by 2009. He held posts as an assistant professor and faculty member at Otani University and the Otani Academic Society.
Makoto Kitada is an Indology and linguistics scholar who completed doctoral studies at the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg. He has held posts at Toho Kenkyukai and Osaka University.

Makoto Nagai was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate from the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at the University of Tokyo, Nihon University, Toyo University, and Kamakura Women's University, and was president of Chuo Shoka Junior College.

Makoto Yoshimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who completed doctoral studies at Waseda University around 1996–2001. He served as an assistant professor at Komazawa University around 2005.

Malcolm David Eckel works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Harvard and Oxford, completing his doctorate under Masatoshi Nagatomi, and held posts at Harvard University, Harvard Divinity School, and Boston University.

Mallica Kumbera Landrus works in Indology and art history and archaeology. She serves as Associate Professor of Indian Art and Keeper of Eastern Art at the Ashmolean Museum of Art and Archaeology, affiliated with the University of Oxford and Wolfson College.
Mamata Dash is an Indology scholar who was educated at Ravenshaw Girls' School and Utkal University.

Mamoru Tonami was a scholar of Sinology and history who earned his degrees, including a doctorate, from Kyoto University. He spent his career primarily at Kyoto University from 1965 to 2001, also holding posts at Kobe University and Otani University.
Manabendu Banerjee is an Indologist who served as secretary of The Asiatic Society. He also served as Co-ordinator for DSA Sanskrit at Jadavpur University.
Manabu Asano is a Buddhist studies researcher who pursued doctoral studies at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies. He has held a researcher post at Minobusan University.
